items.followUp: Write the ASCII codes of any two lowercase letters.

rubric.why: Awards credit for one correct ASCII code for a digit character.
rubric.description: Gives the ASCII code for the character 0.
rubric.how: Check that the student pairs 0 with 48.

rubric.why: Awards credit for a second correct ASCII code for a digit character.
rubric.description: Gives the ASCII code for the character 1.
rubric.how: Check that the student pairs 1 with 49.

items.followUp: Define the decimal number system and state its base.

rubric.why: Identifies the base of the binary system.
rubric.description: States that the binary system has base 2.
rubric.how: Look for the key result base 2 or radix 2.

rubric.why: Names the symbols used in binary representation.
rubric.description: States that binary uses only the digits 0 and 1.
rubric.how: Check that both 0 and 1 are stated as its digits.

modelAnswer: The binary system is a number system with base 2.
It uses only the digits 0 and 1.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table of the OR operator.

rubric.why: Checks the AND output when both inputs are 0.
rubric.how: Check the truth-table row A=0, B=0, output=0.

rubric.why: Checks the remaining AND truth-table rows.
rubric.description: Gives outputs 0, 0, and 1 for inputs 01, 10, and 11.
rubric.how: Check all three remaining input-output rows.

items.followUp: Write the complement law of Boolean algebra.

rubric.description: States that OR with 0 leaves the variable unchanged.
rubric.how: Look for A + 0 = A or its equivalent.

rubric.description: States that AND with 1 leaves the variable unchanged.
rubric.how: Look for A · 1 = A or its equivalent.

items.followUp: What is the use of HTTP?

rubric.description: States that FTP is used to transfer files.
rubric.how: Look for the key idea of file transfer.

rubric.why: Specifies where or how the file transfer takes place.
rubric.description: States that files are transferred between computers over a network.
rubric.how: Look for computers and a network, or an equivalent description.

modelAnswer: FTP is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
It can be used to upload and download files.

items.followUp: Name the two versions of IP currently used for addressing.

rubric.why: Checks the number of IP addressing standards.
rubric.description: States that there are two IP addressing standards.

rubric.why: Checks that both standards are named.
rubric.how: Check that both version names appear.

modelAnswer: There are two IP addressing standards.

items.followUp: Encrypt the word “CAT” using a Caesar cipher with a shift of three letters.

rubric.why: Checks the Caesar cipher shift used.
rubric.description: States that each letter is shifted forward by three places.
rubric.how: Look for a shift of three.

rubric.description: Gives KWPO as the encryption of HTML.

modelAnswer: Using a Caesar cipher shift of 3: H → K, T → W, M → P, L → O.

items.followUp: Explain why HTML tags are generally written in lowercase.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of case insensitivity.
rubric.description: States that HTML does not distinguish between uppercase and lowercase letters in its syntax.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that letter case does not matter.

rubric.why: Checks that the student describes how differently cased forms are treated.
rubric.description: Explains that uppercase and lowercase forms of an HTML tag are treated as the same.
rubric.how: Look for an example or explicit comparison of letter cases.

modelAnswer: HTML is not case sensitive, so uppercase and lowercase letters in HTML tags are treated as the same.
For example, <HTML> and <html> represent the same tag.
